correctness.rationale: Substitution of (z,v) into the weight-zero identity forces the offcentral vector u to vanish by nondegeneracy of the alternating form. The remaining identity is equivalent to (A-cI)^TJ(A-cI)=c^2J in all characteristics. For nonzero c this is a symplectic group times a torus, with free ell; for c=0 it is the irreducible isotropic-image locus. The dual polynomial identity separates the closure from a rank-two special-fiber witness for n>=2. For n=1 every singular matrix is a degeneration of c-nonzero solutions. Thus exactly one component for n=1 and two for n>=2, with dimensions computed from Sp and the Lagrangian Grassmannian. Exact counts use isotropic flags and surjections. The standalone checker passed exhaustive direct tests over F2/F3 for n=1 and exhaustive A,c tests for n=2 over F2. Finite tests are not substituted for proof.

originality.rationale: The three-dimensional weight-zero classification in Ji--Hua (2018) overlaps only the n=1 specialization and is expressly credited. Rathee (2024) analyzes weight-one operators on the three-dimensional case. Gao--Liu--Bai--Jing (2014) treats homogeneous operators on Witt/Virasoro rather than higher Heisenberg algebras. The verified local research comparisons include Nijenhuis operators on Heisenberg algebras (sharing only the isotropic-image branch), but do not imply the symplectic branch or the two-component reduced variety. Database searches for the shift identity, aliases and dimensions located no dominating claim. The possible relation to symplectic matrix-monoid geometry was assessed through the dual constraint; that closure omits the exhibited special-fiber point. Bounded-search originality, not absolute priority.

value.rationale: This is a complete natural geometric dichotomy for Rota--Baxter operators, including the exact first reducibility threshold, both component dimensions, a higher-rank dimension crossover, and exact cardinalities over all finite fields. The dual obstruction gives a meaningful structural reason why the familiar symplectic-similitude family fails to exhaust degenerations; the theorem controls entire higher-dimensional families rather than an ad hoc small numerical slice.
